summary: The single biggest pattern this week is the mounting pressure on Asian supply chains caused by escalating Red Sea shipping disruptions and crude oil prices surging past $100 per barrel, which are driving up ocean freight rates and bunker fuel surcharges. To counter these external shockwaves, India and China are advancing a high-stakes diplomatic thaw at the BRICS Summit aimed at easing bilateral trade friction, accelerating local-currency settlements, and securing energy supply routes. Moving forward, expect logistics operators to increasingly leverage alternative transport corridors and dynamic fuel surcharges to maintain margin stability amid ongoing maritime security risks.
